nodes.summary: In three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$, write $\bar B(c, r)$ for the closed ball of radius $r$ about $c$. There are points $c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $\bar B(c_1, 1)$ and $\bar B(c_2, 1)$ are disjoint and the closed unit ball $\bar B(0, 1)$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $\bar B(c_1, 1) \cup \bar B(c_2, 1)$.
nodes.title: Banach–Tarski paradox for the closed unit ball

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a metric space $X$. Then $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B$ if and only if there are a map $f : X \to X$ and a finite set $S$ of isometric bijections of $X$ onto itself such that $f$ restricts to a bijection from $A$ onto $B$ and for every $x \in A$ there is $g \in S$ with $f(x) = g(x)$.
nodes.title: Equidecomposability via piecewise-isometric bijections

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space. Subsets $A$ and $B$ of $X$ are finitely equidecomposable by isometries if there are a natural number $n$, sets $A_1, \dots, A_n$ and $B_1, \dots, B_n$ in $X$, and isometric bijections $g_1, \dots, g_n$ of $X$ onto itself such that the sets $A_i$ are pairwise disjoint, the sets $B_i$ are pairwise disjoint, $A = A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_n$, $B = B_1 \cup \dots \cup B_n$, and $g_i(A_i) = B_i$…
nodes.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an isometric bijection of a metric space $X$ onto itself. Then every subset $A$ of $X$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with its image $g(A)$.
nodes.title: Equidecomposability of a set with its isometric image

nodes.summary: Every subset $A$ of a metric space $X$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with itself.
nodes.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries is reflexive

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a metric space $X$. If $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B$, then $B$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $A$.
nodes.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries is symmetric

nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be subsets of a metric space $X$. If $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B$ and $B$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $C$, then $A$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $C$.
nodes.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries is transitive

nodes.summary: Let $A_1$, $A_2$, $B_1$ and $B_2$ be subsets of a metric space $X$ with $A_1 \cap A_2 = \emptyset$ and $B_1 \cap B_2 = \emptyset$. If $A_1$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B_1$ and $A_2$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B_2$, then $A_1 \cup A_2$ is finitely equidecomposable by isometries with $B_1 \cup B_2$.
nodes.title: Finite equidecomposability by isometries respects disjoint unions

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
